mainTopic: Why the משנה needs each of its 'הפה שאסר' and captive-woman cases, and whether רבי יהודה and the רבנן worry about גומלין (people vouching for each other).
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why the משנה needs each of its 'הפה שאסר' cases: the two money cases, and the married woman who says she is divorced, which is an איסור. It then asks why the משנה needs each of the following cases. The captive woman who says she is pure is a lead-in: either to the rule about witnesses who come after she marries, or to the case of two captured women. The case of two captured women teaches that we do not worry about גומלין, people vouching for each other in exchange. The case of two men who say they are כהנים is there to open the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן. A ברייתא spells out that argument: the רבנן believe the men for תרומה, but רבי יהודה does not. The גמרא then points out that in a משנה about donkey drivers the two sides seem to hold the opposite views about גומלין. רב answers that the names are switched in one source. אביי answers that רבי יהודה is lenient only with דמאי. רבא adds that the רבנן are not contradicting themselves either, because the donkey-drivers case involves a man with the tools of his trade in hand; that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the reason the money cases are both needed
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the previous argument: without the other case, we would have said the claim is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started just before this section. It is explaining why one money case of 'הפה שאסר' cannot be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument says: if the משנה had taught only one of the money cases, we might have thought the rule does not cover the other one. These words close that thought. They show that each money case teaches something of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: I would say no; we might have thought the rule does not apply
it is needed; the גמרא's way of explaining why each case in a list is necessary

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the tail end of an argument that began before this section, so read it as the end of the earlier sentence.

phrases.english: say no.
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier sentence: had we learned only the other case, we'd have thought this claim isn't believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא argument that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case is needed
steps.terutzMaskana: Each money case of 'הפה שאסר' teaches something the other could not.

steps.title: Why the married-woman case is also needed
steps.stepSummary: The two money cases cannot teach us about a married woman who says she is divorced, because that case is about an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only these two cases, one could say they are believed because they are about money. But a married woman is a matter of איסור, so I would say she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה also needs the case of a woman who says, 'I was married and I am divorced.' Without it, we might think the rule works only for money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Courts are more relaxed about money than about איסור. So believing someone about money does not prove we would believe a woman about אשת איש, which is a very serious איסור. That is why the משנה needs to state this third case on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: a matter of איסור (what is forbidden or permitted)

steps.whatToRemember: All three 'הפה שאסר' cases are needed. Two are about money, and the married-woman case shows the rule works even for a serious איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of הפה שאסר is not limited to money. It applies even to the serious איסור of אשת איש.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us these two,
phrases.notes: These two are the money cases just discussed.

phrases.english: that is because it is money;
but a married woman, which is a matter of איסור —
say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries on the same צריכותא argument and finishes it by explaining the third case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: a difference between money and איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think a person is believed only about money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The married-woman case is needed to show she is believed even about איסור.

steps.title: Why teach the case of the captive woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the case of 'I was captured and I am pure.' It seems to add nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I was taken captive and I am pure': why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the next case in the משנה and asks why it is there at all. If the same rule was already taught, this case looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The married-woman case already showed that הפה שאסר works even for a serious איסור. A captive woman claiming she stayed pure looks like the same rule applied one more time, so the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: I am pure; no one violated me in captivity
why do I need it? (a challenge saying something is extra)

phrases.english: 'I was taken captive and I am pure'
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first three cases, the גמרא challenges the need for the next one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of 'נשביתי וטהורה אני'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of הפה שאסר was already taught, even for איסור, so this case seems to add nothing.

steps.title: It sets up the rule about witnesses coming later
steps.stepSummary: The captive case is taught so the משנה can add: if witnesses come after she marries, she does not have to leave her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wanted to teach: 'And if witnesses came after she married, she does not leave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the captive case is not there for its own sake. It is there to set up the rule that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new lesson is the rule about witnesses. If witnesses later say she was captured after she has already married, she may stay with her husband. That rule needs the captive case before it, so the משנה includes the captive case.

phrases.english: Because he wanted to teach:
'And if the witnesses came after she married —
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who say she was captured.

phrases.english: she does not leave.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is a lead-in for a later rule
steps.terutzMaskana: It is needed as the setup for the rule about witnesses coming after she marries.

steps.title: That answer works only for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the opinion that the witnesses rule belongs to the captive case. But some say it belongs to the married-woman case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who teaches it on the later clause. But for the one who teaches it on the first clause, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. There is a disagreement about which case the witnesses rule belongs to, and the answer only works for one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some put the rule about witnesses on the married-woman case, not the captive case. For them, the captive case does not set up anything. It also seems obvious: if a woman is believed about the very serious איסור of אשת איש, she should surely be believed about the lighter איסור of a captive marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: for the one who teaches it (attaches the rule to)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who teaches it on the later clause,
phrases.notes: The later clause is the captive-woman case.

phrases.english: but for the one who teaches it on the first clause —
phrases.notes: The first clause is the woman who says she was married and is divorced.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the captive case sets up the witnesses rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that attaches the witnesses rule to the רישא, the captive case sets up nothing and is still extra.

steps.title: It sets up the case of two captured women
steps.stepSummary: Even for that opinion, the captive case is taught as a lead-in to the משנה's next case of two women who were captured.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he wanted to teach: 'Two women who were taken captive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an answer that works for both opinions. The captive case opens the door to the next case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to discuss two women who were captured and what each says about the other. To get there, it first states the simple case of one captive woman. So the captive case is a setup, not an extra.

keyTerms.meaning: two women who were taken captive

steps.whatToRemember: The 'נשביתי וטהורה אני' case is in the משנה as a lead-in. One answer says it leads into the witnesses rule. The answer that works for everyone says it leads into the case of two captive women.

phrases.english: Because he wanted to teach:
'Two women who were taken captive.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁנִּשְׁבּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 with a reason that works for both opinions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is a lead-in for the next case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For the רישא opinion, the captive case seemed to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: It introduces the משנה's case of two captive women.

steps.title: Why teach the case of two captured women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the case of two women who were captured, since we already know one captive woman is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to teach the case of two women who were captured?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps checking each case in the משנה. Now it asks what the case of two captured women adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that a captive woman who says 'I am pure' is believed. If one woman is believed about herself, it seems obvious that two women vouching for each other are believed too. So the case looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking what a case adds)

phrases.english: And "two women who were captured"
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 said the captive case leads into the two-women case. Now the גמרא asks why the two-women case itself is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of two captured women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one woman is believed about herself, two women vouching for each other should obviously be believed. The case seems to add nothing.

steps.title: No worry that the women are covering for each other
steps.stepSummary: The case teaches that we do not suspect the two women of trading favors, each vouching for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we should worry that they are returning favors to each other. So the משנה teaches us that we do not worry about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two women are different from one woman. They might be helping each other, and the משנה teaches that we are not worried about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two women, there is a new worry: 'You say I am pure, and I will say you are pure.' This is called גומלין. The משנה teaches that we do not suspect this, so both are believed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
Returning favors: each one helps the other in exchange

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of גומלין becomes the main theme for the rest of this section.

phrases.english: You might have said
let us worry about them returning favors,
phrases.notes: Meaning each woman says 'she is pure' so the other will say the same about her.

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that we do not worry).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new point the case teaches (a חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have suspected the two women of גומלין and not believed them.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about גומלין here; both women are believed.

steps.title: Why teach the case of two men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה adds 'and so too two men', since the two-women case already taught that we do not worry about גומלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to say 'and so too two men'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה: two men who each say the other is a כהן. It asks what this adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two-women case already taught that we do not suspect people of vouching for each other. The case of two men seems to teach the same thing again.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too two men (the next case in the משנה)

phrases.english: "And so too two men"
phrases.notes: In the משנה, each man says 'I am a כהן and my friend is a כהן.'

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 7, now about the next case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of two men
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that we do not worry about גומלין was already taught by the two women, so the two men add nothing.

steps.title: The two men are a lead-in to an argument
steps.stepSummary: The case of two men is taught so the משנה can bring the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to teach the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two-men case does not teach a new rule by itself. It is there to open the argument that follows in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to bring a disagreement between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about men claiming to be כהנים. To set that up, it first states the case of two men.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה and the Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: Because he wants to teach
the argument of רבי יהודה and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9, the same way step 6 answered for the captive case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case serves as a lead-in to the next teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-men case seemed to repeat the two-women case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is taught to open the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא: two men who say they are both כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the רבנן believe two men vouching for each other for eating תרומה but not for marrying, while רבי יהודה does not believe them even for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a man says 'I am a כהן and my friend is a כהן', he is believed to let his friend eat תרומה. But he is not believed to let him marry a woman (as a כהן with proper lineage) until there are three people, so that two testify about this one and two testify about that one. רבי יהודה says: He is not believed even to let him eat תרומה until there are three, so that two testify about this one and two testify about that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן mentioned in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say that for תרומה, each man's word about the other is enough. For marriage, which needs proper lineage, they want two full witnesses for each man, so a third person must join. רבי יהודה wants the three-person setup even for תרומה, which looks like he suspects the two men of vouching for each other.

keyTerms.meaning: To let him eat תרומה, which only כהנים may eat
To let him marry a woman as a כהן with proper lineage

steps.confusionAlert: With three people, each man gets two witnesses: the third person plus his friend. That is how three people give 'two about this one and two about that one.'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"I am a כהן and my friend is a כהן" —
he is believed to let him eat תרומה,
but he is not believed to let him marry a woman
until there are three:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם מְעִידִין עַל זֶה, וּשְׁנַיִם מְעִידִין עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: two testify about this one, and two testify about that one.
רבי יהודה says:
he is not believed even to let him eat תרומה
until there are three,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם מְעִידִין עַל זֶה וּשְׁנַיִם מְעִידִין עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: two testify about this one and two testify about that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the full text of the argument that step 10 said the משנה wanted to teach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: two men vouching for each other are believed for תרומה but not for marriage. רבי יהודה: they are not believed even for תרומה without a third person.

steps.title: The donkey drivers seem to show the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests רבי יהודה worries about גומלין and the רבנן do not, but a משנה about donkey drivers suggests the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יהודה worries about returning favors, and the רבנן do not? But we heard the opposite from them! As we learned in a משנה: Donkey drivers came into a city, and one of them said: 'Mine is new and my friend's is old,' or 'Mine is not tithed and my friend's is tithed.' He is not believed. רבי יהודה says: He is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא about who worries about גומלין, then challenges it with a משנה where the opinions seem flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the donkey-drivers case, one driver praises his friend's produce, and in the next city the friend may praise his. The רבנן say he is not believed, so they seem to worry about גומלין. רבי יהודה says he is believed, so he seems not to worry, which is the opposite of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (draws a conclusion to question it)
We heard the opposite from them

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'mine is new, my friend's is old' runs down his own produce. That makes him seem honest, which is exactly why there is a worry he is just doing his friend a favor.

phrases.english: Is that to say that רבי יהודה worries about returning favors,
and the Rabbis do not worry about returning favors?
But we heard the opposite from them,
as we learned in a משנה:
Donkey drivers who came into a city,
and one of them said:
"Mine is new, and my friend's is old";
phrases.notes: Old, dried produce was worth more, so he is praising his friend's goods over his own.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלִּי אֵינוֹ מְתוּקָּן, וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרִי מְתוּקָּן —
phrases.english: "Mine is not tithed, and my friend's is tithed" —
he is not believed.
רבי יהודה says: he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the ברייתא in step 11 and attacks it with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding that רבי יהודה worries about גומלין and the רבנן do not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the donkey-drivers משנה, the רבנן do not believe the driver (worrying about גומלין) and רבי יהודה does believe him (not worrying). Each side seems to contradict its own view in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב: The names in one source are switched
steps.stepSummary: רב answers the contradiction by saying the opinions in one of the sources are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the contradiction from step 12. רב says that in one of the two sources the names of רבי יהודה and the רבנן should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are swapped, each side holds the same view in both cases. Whoever worries about גומלין worries in both cases, and whoever does not worry does not worry in either. This removes the contradiction by fixing the text, not by finding a difference between the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The line of opinions, meaning which name goes with which view

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: He means that in one of the two sources, רבי יהודה's name and the רבנן's name should trade places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and the רבנן hold opposite views about גומלין in the two cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source has the names switched, so each opinion stays the same in both cases.

steps.title: אביי: Keep the names; דמאי is a lenient case
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the text as it is and explains that רבי יהודה is lenient only with דמאי, because most עמי הארץ do tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, do not switch the names. The חכמים were lenient with דמאי, because most עמי הארץ do tithe their produce.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer and leaves the text alone. He explains why רבי יהודה believes the donkey driver even though he usually worries about גומלין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is only a rabbinic safety measure, since most עמי הארץ really do tithe. So even weak testimony is enough to permit the produce. רבי יהודה still worries about גומלין in general, as in the כהנים case, but he is lenient here because the concern about דמאי is weak to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (it stays as first stated)
Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed
People who are not careful about the laws of tithes and purity

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, do not reverse it.
With doubtfully tithed produce they were lenient,
since most amei ha'aretz do tithe.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying that רבי יהודה ignores גומלין. He still worries about it in general and makes an exception only for דמאי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns down רב's switch and offers a different answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (leniency special to דמאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's view in the donkey-drivers case shows he does not worry about גומלין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does worry about גומלין but is lenient in the special case of דמאי.

steps.title: רבא: The רבנן's side is still unsolved
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that אביי only explained רבי יהודה and left the contradiction in the רבנן unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is only the contradiction in רבי יהודה a problem, and the contradiction in the רבנן not a problem?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer. The רבנן also seem to contradict themselves, and אביי did not deal with that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כהנים case the רבנן do not worry about גומלין, yet in the donkey-drivers case they do. The דמאי leniency cannot explain this, because there the רבנן are the strict ones. So אביי's answer is only half an answer.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda difficult,
while the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. רבא means the רבנן's contradiction is just as much a problem.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The דמאי leniency explains only רבי יהודה. The רבנן are strict about גומלין with the donkey drivers but lenient with the כהנים, and that is still unexplained.

steps.title: רבא: Neither side contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבי יהודה as above and begins explaining the רבנן using רבי חמא בר עוקבא's case of someone holding his work tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה does not contradict himself, as we explained. The רבנן do not contradict themselves either, as רבי חמא בר עוקבא said: it is a case where he has the tools of his trade in his hand,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own full answer. For רבי יהודה he uses אביי's דמאי answer. For the רבנן he starts to explain that the donkey-drivers case is a special situation, where the man has his work tools in hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן normally do not worry about גומלין, as in the כהנים case. In the donkey-drivers case, though, the situation of a man with the tools of his trade in hand makes them suspicious. The text breaks off here, and the גמרא will go on to explain how this teaching applies.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rather: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult,
as we explained.
phrases.notes: This points back to אביי's answer that the חכמים were lenient with דמאי.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult,
as Rabbi Ḥama bar Ukva said,
where the tools of his trade are in his hand,

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: רבי יהודה does worry about גומלין but is lenient with דמאי. The רבנן do not worry about גומלין, except in a special case like a man holding the tools of his trade.
